cells.tense: You are keeping two growing things alive at once, and both are getting what they need.
cells.ask: Hand one growing thing to someone else this week and tell them what it needs, not how to do it.
cells.core:
Two things need you at the same time and neither one is going short. Some days that looks like planning, some days like saying no to something reasonable, and underneath it is care with a spine in it. You also know which light you are walking toward. You picked it out and you have not swapped it for whatever was brightest that week. Nothing here is being forced. Things are coming along at the speed they come along, and you are the one who keeps the conditions right.

It holds only while this stays yours to give. The next thing it can feed is a handover — finishing something small, letting it run without you, and letting the finish count.
cells.sheetLine: You keep two things growing and neither one goes without.
cells.verb: Giving what is still growing a form it can hold
cells.place: On the way toward a light you have already picked out and cannot yet stand in

cells.tense: You are already past the harvest in your head, braced for a loss that has not happened.
cells.ask: Put the unfinished thing away for a day and spend the time on something already done.
cells.core:
Ahead of you is a picture of how this turns out, and you are already standing in it, so every part that has not arrived yet reads as a warning. You water more than the plant can drink. You redo what was already fine. The attention is doing its work; the hold is the part that costs, because a thing gripped that hard cannot go its own direction. The light you set out toward has not moved. What moved is that you keep checking the distance instead of walking it.

The way back is not less care. It is care that lets things finish, so the dreaming starts from something completed instead of something still owed.

cells.tense: The offering stopped at some point and you are still standing at that closed door.
cells.ask: Water one plant and write today's date on a slip of paper beside it.
cells.core:
You know what it looks like when something gets what it needs. These days the things around you get managed instead of grown — kept alive, kept tidy, kept at a distance — and the pull toward what you actually want has gone quiet. Not gone. Quiet. You still know which light you picked. What is missing is the habit of walking toward it with your hands out.

Strength comes back through hope here, not through effort, so start smaller than seems worth it. One thing tended, one mark that it happened, and let the row of marks be the evidence before any feeling shows up.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped caring for growing things, and the quiet is not peace.

cells.tense: You are already bringing something into shape and calling it the situation.
cells.ask: Say out loud, about one thing you brought this far, that you did that.
cells.core:
Look at what is growing around you and look at who arranged the conditions — the timing, the people, the order things happened in. The room did not organise itself. You have been steering this for a while, and the steering has been steady enough that it stopped registering as yours. The direction is real, the light you picked is real, and the credit is going to nobody. Worth noticing, not because you need praise, but because a thing you will not name is a thing you cannot decide to keep doing or stop.

What comes with the naming is release. Something finishes, you let it finish, and the completion is allowed to be yours.

attempts.check: The draft risks saying the person feels responsible for others' growth as a fact about them; the record only shows care-through-form operating in a moment, so the reader could fairly answer that the tending is practical logistics, not nurturing. The asks survive a wrong read because each is one visible act — handing a pot over, closing the shelf, writing two words on paper, saying 'I did that' — useful whether or not the diagnosis lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying they are hiding from their own lightness; cut it and keep the mechanism in the open.
